newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Absa gets win in attempt to bring Askin to SAfrica.
newsitem.headline: Absa gets win in attempt to bring Askin to SAfrica.

text.p: Amalgamated banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) said on Friday that it had secured a legal win in its attempts to bring former Tollgate Holdings head Julian Askin to stand trial on fraud charges in South Africa.
Tollgate, a mini-conglomerate headed by Askin, collapsed in 1992 leaving major banker Bankorp with an exposure of 200 million rand in bad debt. Absa took over Bankorp in September, 1992.
Absa said Britain's High Court had ruled that Askin's case should be tried in South Africa and refused Askin leave to appeal to the Court of Appeal.

"The court granted the entirety of the applications made by Absa and the other defendants to stay Mr Askin's proceedings on the grounds that his action should more appropriately be tried in South Africa," the bank said in statement.
An Absa spokeswoman said Askin could still ask the Court of Appeal to hear his case -- in short he can still appeal for an appeal.
"He can appeal to the Court of Appeal and they can still give him leave to appeal," she said.
In 1995 an Italian court agreed to extradite Askin back to South Africa from Florence, but Askin had moved to London before the decision was handed down.

Askin, who faces eight charges of fraud totalling 29 million rand, spent two months in Florence's Solliciano jail before being released into house arrest for health reasons. The house arrest order was then lifted and he moved to London several months later.
